sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.intro: Employer identity providers (SAML or OIDC). A connection starts as a draft, moves to testing once a domain is verified, and becomes active after a test sign-in.
sso.sampleNote: Sample data: these connections are fictional. Nothing can be created, tested or changed in sample mode.
sso.jitWarning: JIT creates an account for anyone the identity provider asserts on a verified domain.

create.title: New SSO connection
create.description: The connection starts as a draft. Nothing is sent to the identity provider until you test it, except an OIDC client secret, which is handed over straight away.
create.slugHint: 2 to 11 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. It builds the provider name and cannot change later.
create.secretHint: Write-only: kept by the identity provider and never shown again. Needed before the first test.
create.oidcClaimRequired: Require a verified email claim from the provider
create.oidcClaimRequiredHint: Turn off only after the client confirms that its email claim is the directory's verified address.
create.defaultOrgUnitHint: Optional. Accounts created on first sign-in join this org unit.

edit.title: Edit connection
edit.description: Only the fields you change are sent.
edit.protocolLocked: The protocol can change only while the connection is a draft.
edit.secretReplaceHint: Leave empty to keep the current secret. The secret is never shown.
edit.metadataXmlHint: Leave empty to keep the current XML.
edit.activeWarning: This connection is active. Changing the provider settings (metadata, issuer, client ID or client secret) takes it back to testing: sign-in through this connection stays off for employees until a new test sign-in succeeds and you activate it again.
edit.suspendedWarning: This connection is suspended. Changing the provider settings (metadata, issuer, client ID or client secret) moves it to testing: it stays off until a new test sign-in succeeds and you activate it.
edit.backToTesting: Changes saved. The connection is back in testing: run a test sign-in, then activate it again.

actions.testNote: Open the link in a new tab and complete the workspace sign-in with an account on a verified domain (you land on the workspace as that account), then come back here and select Activate.
actions.suspendDescription: Sign-in no longer sends people to {{provider}}; they use the email code until the connection is reactivated.
actions.resetConfirm: Resetting deletes the provider {{provider}} registered at the identity provider and clears the last test sign-in. Domains and settings stay. For an OIDC connection, enter the client secret again (Edit) before the next test.
